newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Manitoba posts Q2 deficit of C$107.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Manitoba posts Q2 deficit of C$107.1 mln.

text.p: The Canadian province of Manitoba said on Wednesday it posted a deficit of C$107.1 million in the first six months of fiscal 1996/97 (Apr/Mar) but forecast a second consecutive budget surplus for the year of C$36 million.
The deficit up to Sept 30 was C$47.9 million less than forecast mainly due to the timing of expenses and revenues, the provincial government statement said.

"Manitoba's economy continues to perform well above the national average and this strength is reflected in these positive adjustments to our revenues," Manitoba Finance Minister Eric Stefanson said in the statement.
The forecast C$36 million surplus for all of fiscal 1996.97 exceeded an earlier projection of C$21.8 million by C$14.2 million, it said.
The adjustments stem from an expected C$63.9 million rise in revenues and a C$49.7 million rise in expenditures.
Most of the rise in revenue is due to prior year adjustments for corporate and individual income taxes from Manitoba's strong economic performance in 1995, he said.
The rise in expenses was due to spring flooding, forest fire suppression and health care.
The year-end forecast does not include revenues from the sale of the government owned telephone firm Manitoba Telephone System.

Net revenue from the sale of MTS, after paying down its C$400 million debt, will be taken into the consolidated revenue fund and transferred to Manitoba's fiscal stabilization fund, a "rainy day" account.
